text:
Sara (ML Eng): quick heads-up — finished the quant-sensitivity sweep for nyx13b across our GTN slices. posting a compact readout + recommended acceptance/checklist for product rollout.
James (Product): awesome — high level first: is int6 viable as default? what are the hit areas?
Sara (ML Eng): short answer: yes for most chat/short-answer slices. caveats for long-context retrieval/rerank. detail dump below.
Sara (ML Eng): raw sweep summary (all numbers averaged across 3 runs per slice):
```
model variant | cost factor vs fp16 | latency p50 | latency p95 | R@10 (retrieval) | human helpfulness (binary, % pass)
nyx13b-fp16  | 1.0                 | 120ms      | 340ms      | 0.78             | 87%
nyx13b-int8  | 0.55                | 110ms      | 300ms      | 0.76             | 86%
nyx13b-int6  | 0.42                | 105ms      | 320ms      | 0.71             | 80%
nyx13b-int4  | 0.30                | 100ms      | 360ms      | 0.60             | 62%
```
Notes: cost factor computed as token-TCO proxy (GPU sec * price normalized). latency measured on our dedicated pool with 8k max seq and batching similar to production. R@10 is retrieval recall on GTN longform slice (2000 queries). human helpfulness from blind eval (n=400).

Kevin (DevEx): thanks — that p95 for int6 looks a bit tight vs int8 (320ms vs 300ms) — same batch config?
Sara (ML Eng): same batch config. higher p95 for int6 caused by kernel variability on long sequences and extra corrective iterations in KV cache handling. p50 improves though (warm cache benefits).
Anya (GTN): so for end-user impact: what % of our traffic is "longform retrieval" vs short-chat?
James (Product): ~12% longform/rerank heavy (docs, search), ~65% short Q/A/chat, ~23% other (summaries, code). For the 12% we shouldn't degrade >5% R@10 or user-facing NPS.
Sara (ML Eng): recommended rollout plan: 
- Phase 0 (internal): int6 for canary on non-critical channels (5% traffic) for 48h. acceptance: no >3% drop in short-chat human helpfulness and <5% customer errors.
- Phase 1 (GToN shadow): int6 for 25% of short-chat traffic shadowed for metrics; default remains int8 for longform. check: retrieval R@10 delta <= 4% for longform slice; automated evals pass.
- Phase 2 (gradual): if Phase1 OK, promote int6 to 60% of short-chat traffic; keep int8 for rerank/longform.
- Fallback: route requests scoring >L (long prompt length or high rerank weight) to int8 automatically (routing flag based on tokens >1500 or rerank=True).

Kevin (DevEx): routing flag idea is easy — we'll add `quant_variant_hint` in request metadata and a server-side policy: if tokens>1500 or rerank==true -> prefer int8. I'll prototype a canary config.
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: nyx13b-int6 image -> canary pool at 2026-04-05T08:00Z (auto rollback on >1% error spike).
Anya (GTN): acceptance criteria for GTN handoff to product: 
- Unit econ: int6 should show >=1.9x cost reduction vs fp16 on short-chat buckets.
- Quality: aggregated user helpfulness delta <= -3% vs int8 for short-chat.
- Safety/regression: no new toxicity regression above baseline (automated checks).

Sara (ML Eng): empirical unit-econ quick calc from sweep: median token cost proxy: fp16 $1.00/unit -> int8 $0.55/unit -> int6 $0.42/unit. For 65% traffic short-chat, expected gross savings ~26% platform-wide if we adopt int6 for short-chat only.
James (Product): good — spell that out for commercial: we'll need a <1-page blurb for GTN recommending default quant variant by workload and a short FAQ for customers on latency/quality tradeoffs. Anya can you own the blurb?
Anya (GTN): got it — I'll draft. need a small table for "how we decide per request" (tokens, rerank flag, criticality).
Sara (ML Eng): practical acceptance test snippets for eval infra: 
```bash
# run synthetic regression against golden prompts
./eval_run.sh --model nyx13b-int6 --slices gtn_short_chat,gtn_longform --seed 42 --report /tmp/int6_report.json
# compare
python tools/compare_eval.py --base /tmp/int8_baseline.json --new /tmp/int6_report.json --thresholds '{"helpfulness": -0.03, "r@10": -0.05}'
```
Kevin (DevEx): will wire those into the canary pipeline so the compare step gates promotion. can also emit a slack summary bot message on pass/fail.
James (Product): one more ask: can we get a tiny ablation for mixed-precision where we run int6 for prompt encoding + int8 for generation? any quick wins?
Sara (ML Eng): we tried a hybrid where first N tokens in fp16 then switch to int6 for decoding — complexity high, marginal gains ~3% cost improvement vs full int6 but fewer regressions; not worth the infra churn right now. documented in the long notes.
Anya (GTN): timeline: draft blurb by Thu, internal canary Fri, public note next week if all green.
Sara (ML Eng): action items: 1) Kevin: create canary config + add `quant_variant_hint` routing (PR target EOD tomorrow). 2) Ops: schedule canary as ops-bot noted. 3) Anya: draft GTN blurb. 4) Sara: push full sweep artifacts to S3 + attach to the canary PR.
Kevin (DevEx): on it. PR link when ready.
James (Product): thanks team. If Phase0 shows unexpected quality drops we revert to int8 and loop on quant tuning (maybe try int6 with refined kernel params).
Sara (ML Eng): noted. saving long logs and golden samples to s3://redwood-evals/nyx13b/3348901234/ — will attach to PR.
Anya (GTN): thanks — will draft the customer-facing guidance to emphasize that short-chat is the fast win and longform stays conservative. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: canary started at 2026-04-05T08:00Z on pool canary-nyx13b-int6
